subject.title: [Feature]: Lightweight subagent instruction files (à la Claude Code .claude/agents/)

question: Should OpenClaw core add label-addressed `sessions_spawn` role files with model/tool frontmatter, and what precedence, capability, and audit contract should that trusted surface use?
rationale: The requested behavior is not just prompt text; it can influence model choice, tool visibility, session context, and file trust boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a core role-file contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and design a core sessions_spawn implementation where role files can narrow behavior, explicit spawn args win, and loaded files are exposed for audit.

options.title: Add a plugin seam first
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a generic pre-spawn prompt/config hook so a ClawHub plugin can implement role files without core owning the convention.

options.title: Reject role files for core
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide role-specific subagent personas should stay in explicit task text, full agents.list entries, or external plugins despite the current ergonomics gap.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core role-file contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and design a core sessions_spawn implementation where role files can narrow behavior, explicit spawn args win, and loaded files are exposed for audit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the original sessions_spawn implementation and recent current-main maintenance of the same files.
